title: Legacy TLS 1.0 Negotiated
description: Session negotiated TLS 1.0 which is deprecated by RFC 8996 due to known cryptographic weaknesses.
impact: Exposes traffic to eavesdropping and man-in-the-middle attacks via BEAST, POODLE, and fallback exploits.
recommendation: Disable TLS 1.0 on mail server and client configurations. Enforce TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3.

title: Legacy TLS 1.1 Negotiated
description: Session negotiated TLS 1.1 which is deprecated by RFC 8996 and lacks modern cipher support.
impact: Lacks support for modern authenticated encryption (AEAD) algorithms and weak key exchange.
recommendation: Disable TLS 1.1 on mail server and client configurations. Require minimum TLS 1.2.

title: Obsolete/Unsupported TLS Configuration
description: Session uses SSL 2.0 or SSL 3.0 protocol version.
impact: Severely compromised protocol version vulnerable to DROWN and POODLE attacks.
recommendation: Immediately disable SSLv2 and SSLv3 across all mail endpoints.

title: Weak Cipher Suite Configuration
description: Session negotiated an insecure cipher suite (RC4, 3DES, EXPORT, NULL, or non-AEAD CBC ciphers).
impact: Permits passive decryption of traffic or sweet32 collision attacks.
recommendation: Reconfigure mail server cipher suites to prefer AES-GCM or CHACHA20-POLY1305 AEAD ciphers.

title: Plaintext Email Communication
description: Email session transmitted cleartext commands and messages without TLS or STARTTLS encryption.
impact: Exposes email content, sender/recipient metadata, and credentials to passive network eavesdroppers.
recommendation: Enforce mandatory TLS (implicit TLS on port 465/993/995 or explicit STARTTLS on port 587/25/143/110).

title: STARTTLS Offered But Not Used
description: Server advertised STARTTLS capability in EHLO response, but client continued in cleartext without issuing STARTTLS.
impact: Client transmitted email session in plaintext despite server capability to encrypt transport.
recommendation: Configure mail client to enforce mandatory STARTTLS or fail connection if encryption is available.

title: Potential STARTTLS Downgrade Indicator
description: Observed STARTTLS negotiation error or failure response during session handshake.
impact: May indicate an active adversary stripping STARTTLS advertisements to force cleartext fallback.
recommendation: Enable MTA-STS (RFC 8461) or DANE (RFC 7672) to enforce strict TLS transport security.

title: Expired X.509 Certificate
description: Server presented an X.509 certificate whose notAfter date is in the past.
impact: Invalidates server identity trust, exposing clients to man-in-the-middle interception.
recommendation: Renew and install a valid X.509 certificate immediately.

title: Certificate Validity Problem
description: Certificate validity notBefore date is in the future or date parsing failed.
impact: Indicates improper certificate issuance or clock skew on mail server.
recommendation: Verify system time and re-issue certificate with valid date range.

title: Certificate Hostname Mismatch
description: Server certificate SAN/CN does not match the target mail server domain name.
impact: Clients cannot verify server identity, allowing impersonation attacks.
recommendation: Issue certificate containing exact FQDN in Subject Alternative Name (SAN).

title: Weak Certificate Key Size
description: Server certificate uses RSA key size smaller than 2048 bits.
impact: RSA 1024-bit keys are vulnerable to factorization by well-funded adversaries.
recommendation: Replace certificate with minimum 2048-bit RSA key or ECDSA P-256 key.

title: Weak Certificate Signature Algorithm
description: Certificate signed using deprecated MD5 or SHA-1 hash algorithm.
impact: SHA-1 collision attacks permit forgery of rogue certificates.
recommendation: Re-issue certificate using SHA-256 or SHA-384 signature algorithm.

title: Plaintext Authentication Exposure
description: Authentication credentials (AUTH PLAIN, LOGIN, USER/PASS) transmitted over unencrypted transport.
impact: Direct credential theft allowing total account takeover.
recommendation: Prohibit authentication prior to TLS/STARTTLS establishment.

title: Modern Secure TLS Configuration
description: Session successfully negotiated modern TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3 protocol.
impact: Provides strong confidentiality and integrity protection.

title: Strong Cipher Configuration
description: Session negotiated modern AEAD cipher suite (AES-GCM / CHACHA20-POLY1305).
impact: Ensures authenticated encryption with forward secrecy.
recommendation: Maintain preferred AEAD cipher suite configuration.
